rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns managing and growing wealth or attending to children until one neglects God's remembrance and prefers them over Him; such a person suffers immense loss.
rows.anchor: الانشغال بأمر الأموال والتصرف فيها والسعي في تدبير أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author chose to discuss both verses after being asked why asaddaqu is subjunctive while akun is coordinated in the jussive; their connection warrants treating them together.
rows.anchor: لماذا قال تعالى: {فَأَصَّدَّقَ} بالنصب وعطف بالجزم، فقال: (وأكنْ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilha means distracting, unlike ordinary occupation, which can be praiseworthy, as prayer is described as an occupation and Paradise's people are joyfully occupied; the stronger blameworthy word best suits the warning.
rows.anchor: وكما قال تعالى: {إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الجنة اليوم فِي شُغُلٍ فاكهون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar makes wealth and children the agents forbidden to distract, while believers are the intended people being warned against becoming preoccupied with them.
rows.anchor: والفاعل في الآية هو الأموال والأولاد. أما المخاطبون فمفعول به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical shift parallels the warning that worldly life and the Deceiver not delude people: the apparent target is the cause, while believers are told not to be deceived by it.
rows.anchor: فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic prohibition grammatically targets the agent, as in the examples of telling Mahmoud not to strike Khalid or Ibrahim not to travel.
rows.anchor: نحو قولك: (لا يضربْ محمودٌ خالداً) فـ (محمود) هو المنهي عن أن يضرب خالداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also cites the prohibition against one people mocking another, where the people are the grammatical agents being prohibited.
rows.anchor: ونحو قوله تعالى: {ياأيها الذين آمَنُواْ لاَ يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks why the verse does not use the more natural direct wording, do not be distracted by wealth and children, before explaining the advantages of its shift.
rows.anchor: وقد تقول: ولِمَ لم يعبر بالتعبير الطبيعي فيقول: لا تلتهوا بالأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing wealth and children as the targets of prohibition depicts God protecting the believer by stopping the causes from approaching and distracting him.
rows.anchor: فكأن الله يريد حماية المؤمن وذلك بنهي السبب عن أن يتعرض له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording heightens the warning by depicting money and children as pursuing the believer and seeking to tempt him, so that prohibiting them cuts off the cause of distraction.
rows.anchor: جعل الله المؤمن كأنه مطلوب من قبل الأموال والأولاد تسعى لإلهائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing distraction to wealth and children warns believers to stay alert before they are ensnared without noticing, like the warning not to let someone deceive you.
rows.anchor: أن فيه إهابة للمؤمن ألا يقع في شرك الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor gives wealth deliberate, rational agency, as though it lays a trap to catch the believer.
rows.anchor: إسناد الإلهاء إلى الأموال فجعلها عاقلة مريدة تنصب الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating la before children makes clear that either wealth alone or children alone can distract; joining them under one la could imply only their combination is forbidden.
rows.anchor: كلا من الأموال والأولاد داع من دواعي الإلهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth comes first because pursuing and increasing it consumes much time and can keep someone away from family.
rows.anchor: الانشغال فيها وفي تنميتها يستدعي وقتاً طويلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although children are more valuable than wealth, wealth comes first because this passage concerns distraction, and because the next verse similarly places charity before righteousness.
rows.anchor: 5- قدم المفضول على الفاضل، فالأولاد أفضل من الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Charity precedes being righteous because the context warns against attachment to money: charity removes wealth from hand and heart, while distraction consumes heart, time, and action.
rows.anchor: والصدقة إنما هي إخراج للمال من اليد والقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of remembrance with righteousness is apt because someone distracted from obligations and remembering God is not among the righteous.
rows.anchor: لأن المنشغل عن الفرائض وذكر الله ليس من الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across Quranic pairings, wealth generally precedes children because it more often occupies people or invites display and boasting; he illustrates this with three passages.
rows.anchor: والملاحظ أنه حيث اجتمع المالُ والولد في القرآن الكريم، قُدِّمَ المالُ على الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception puts family before wealth because the context is love: children, spouses, and the other listed relatives collectively matter more than money, and even sons alone outweigh it.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن المقام مقام حب. ولا شك أن المتقدمين من الأبناء والأزواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying whoever does this attributes the distraction to the person's own action and responsibility, affirming that he could turn away from it rather than being a passive victim.
rows.anchor: لينال بذلك جزاءه ولئلا يفهم أنه ليس بمقدور الشخص الانصراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb signals a recurrent, ongoing pattern of distraction, which suits the daily repetition of worldly preoccupation.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على استمرار الحدث وتَكَرُّرهِ ولم يقل: (ومن فعل)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ongoing form also avoids suggesting that one isolated distraction earns this immense loss; repeated conduct better fits the emphatic nominal verdict.
rows.anchor: ليس من المعقول أن يكون ذلك الخسران الكبير الثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss is the fitting outcome because the distracted person seeks profit and growth for wealth, yet trades what is great and lasting for what is base and fleeting.
rows.anchor: العظيمَ الباقي بالحقيرِ الفاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative, separating pronoun, and definite losers together restrict and intensify the verdict: these people are the true and fullest losers, rather than merely sharing some loss.
rows.anchor: بل قال: {فأولائك هُمُ الخاسرون} للدلالة على أنهم هم الخاسرون دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi notes the emphatic restriction created by the demonstrative, the repetition of predication, and the separating pronoun.
rows.anchor: وفي التعريف بالإشارة والحصر للخسران فيهم، وفي تكرير الإسناد وتوسيط ضمير الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance of God is broader than a single ritual such as prayer or jihad: it includes all obligations and inward, spoken, or heart-held remembrance, so the prohibition covers every deed done without God's presence.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن ذكر الله يشمل جميع الفرائض، فكل عمل تعمله لا يكون لله إلا إذا كنت ذاكراً لله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is cited as saying that remembrance here encompasses all obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: جميع الفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to spend answers the hypocrites' instruction to their allies not to support the Messenger's companions; God tells believers to spend instead.
rows.anchor: فانظر كيف قابل النهي بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive min asks for only a portion of one's wealth, easing people's willingness to give, whereas asking for all wealth would provoke withholding and resentment.
rows.anchor: فجاء بـ (من) الدالة على التبعيض ولم يقل: (أنفقوا ما رزقناكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling wealth what God provided reminds people that He owns and granted it, making it easier to give some in obedience and overcome stinginess.
rows.anchor: أسند الرزق إلى نفسه فقال: {مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added min in min qabli marks the temporal starting point close to death, urging people to hurry; without it, the phrase could suggest any earlier time and room to delay.
rows.anchor: فإن (من) هذه تفيد ابتداء الغاية الزمانية، ومعناه الزمن القريب من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because every passing hour could be the hour of death, min qabli calls for immediate repentance and spending instead of procrastination.
rows.anchor: وهي التي ذكرها بقوله: {مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الموت} فانظر حُسْنَ التعبير ودقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the person before death focuses attention on the one who must repent and spend and who will regret when death reaches him.
rows.anchor: فالعناية والاهتمام منصبان على المفعول الذي يأتيه الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa links the death to the request both as immediate sequence and as cause: death reveals the bad outcome and triggers instant regret; thumma delays and wa only joins.
rows.anchor: فجاء بالفاء لجمع معنيي السبب والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate fa suits dropping the vocative ya: at death the speaker has no time for expendable words and rushes to his request.
rows.anchor: التضييع في الكلام فيأتي بـ (يا) بل يريد أن يستعجل في طلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawla is a stronger, more urgent plea and conveys self-reproach, while law is a gentler request and can be a hopeless wish rather than a sincere appeal for return.
rows.anchor: لأن (لولا) أَشَدُّ في الطلب من (لو)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past verb after lawla marks the feared loss as already realized and intensifies the plea; a present verb could imply there is still time, as in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن المحذور وقع في حين أن الفعل المضارع قد يفيد أن الأمر لم يقع بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker asks for only a near, short extension to make up for what he neglected, despite having wasted time without concern for his afterlife.
rows.anchor: فطلب مهلة قصيرة وأجلا قريبا لتدارك ما فات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediate fa, the omitted vocative, emphatic lawla, and the near term all compress the request, revealing the terror of death and the desperate need for little time.
rows.anchor: جاء بالفاء الدالة على قصر الزمن بين إتيان الموت وطلب التأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genuine human request benefits the speaker and averts his own harm, unlike Satan's request to live until Judgment Day so he could mislead Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: فإن طلبَ إبليس لا يريدهُ من أجل نفسه، ولا لأنه محتاجٌ إليه، وإنما يريده ليُضِلَّ ذريةَ آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human speaker explicitly says ni because the sincere, direct request serves himself; Satan's conditional oath is not for his benefit, so his pronoun is omitted and only the kasra signals it.
rows.anchor: فلما كان طلب التأخير لمصلحة الطالب حقاً، وأنه ابتغاء لنفسه على وجه الحقيقة أظهر الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaddaqu is subjunctive after the causal fa, while akun is jussive as the answer to the request, with the understood condition if You delay me, I will be righteous; grammarians call this coordination by meaning or by supposition.
rows.anchor: هذا مما يسميه النحاة (العطف على المعنى) وقد يسمى في غير هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: جمهور السبعة
rows.claim: Most of the Seven readers recite akun in the jussive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور السبعة (وأكن) مجزوماً

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes the jussive as coordinated to the syntactic position of asaddaqu, as though the speaker said: if You delay me, I will give and be righteous.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: (وأكن) مجزوماً على محل (فأصدق) كأنه قيل: إن أخرتني أصدق

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya likewise says akun coordinates to the underlying position, with the implied condition if You delay me, I will give and be righteous.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: عطفاً على الموضع لأن التقدير إن تؤخرني أصّدّق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines two meanings: asaddaqu expresses cause or purpose after fa, while akun is conditional as a response to the request, rather than simply repeating the causal construction.
rows.anchor: ففي الآية الكريمة جاء بالمعطوف عليه على إرادة معنى السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteousness matters more for salvation than charity: a believer without resources to donate can still enter Paradise through righteousness, of which charity is one part.
rows.anchor: فالصلاح أهم من الصدقة ذلك أن الذي ينجي من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person in al-Mu'minun asks to do righteous work, not specifically to give charity; this shows righteousness is the basis of salvation outside a passage about wealth.
rows.anchor: فإنه ذكر الصلاح ولم يذكر الصدقة، لأن الآية لم تقع في سياق الكلام على الأموال وإنفاقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making righteousness a conditional commitment strengthens the promise: the speaker binds himself and takes a firm pledge, fitting the more important request.
rows.anchor: فأعطى الأهم والأولى أسلوب الشرط الدال على القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Charity is placed first because the passage and surrounding surah repeatedly discuss wealth, distraction, and hypocrites discouraging charitable spending.
rows.anchor: والجواب: أن السياق هو في إنفاق الأموال، فقد قال تعالى في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaddaqu has five syllabic units compared with six in atasaddaqu, so the shorter form suits the speaker's request for a short extension.
rows.anchor: فإن مقاطع (فأتصدق) ستة ومقاطع (فأصّدّق) خمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra gemination in asaddaqu, on both sad and dal, adds emphasis and abundance to the charity, implying much giving in the brief period requested.
rows.anchor: ثم إن في (فأصّدّق) تضعيفين أحدهما في الصاد، والآخر في الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened form joins two contextual meanings: a brief extension and abundant charity during that brief period.
rows.anchor: فهذا البناء أفاد معنيين: الأول: قصر المدة وذلك لأنه طلب التأخير مدة قصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether la in the opening oath is taken as negation or affirmation, the surah begins by swearing by Resurrection and the reproachful soul; interpreters connect them because Judgment reveals souls' outcomes.
rows.anchor: إن السورة مبنية على ما ابتدأت به من القسم، فهي مبنية على أحوال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: التبيان في أقسام القرآن
rows.claim: Al-Tibyan explains the pairing as the place of recompense, Resurrection, joined with the place of earning, the soul, where its blame and consequences appear.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (التبيان في أقسام القرآن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is specifically described as self-reproaching because people blame themselves both for rushing into wrong and for delaying good until its opportunity passes; both patterns shape the surah.
rows.anchor: والأمرُ الآخر أنه تعالى لم يقسم بالنفس على صفة الإطلاق، بل أقسم بنفسٍ مخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah sustains its opening focus on Resurrection through repeated scenes of the Last Day and returns to it in the final challenge to revive the dead.
rows.anchor: أما يوم القيامة، فقد تكررت أحواله في السورة في تناسق لطيف، إلى أن ختمت بقوله: {أَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayahsabu al-insan joins the human mind's inward supposition with Resurrection, echoing the opening pairing of the human soul and Judgment.
rows.anchor: والملاحظ في هذا التعبير أنه جمع بين نفس الإنسان ويوم القيامة، أيضاً كما ابتدأت السورة فقال: {أَيَحْسَبُ الإنسان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening negative phrasing can communicate more than a direct, explicit request or affirmation, as in saying one will not insist on a visit.
rows.anchor: بها، كما تقول: لن أُلِحَّ عليك في زيارتنا. فتبلغ بالنفي ما لا تبلغه بالطلب المباشر الصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is omitted and grammarians supply you will surely be resurrected; omission fits the haste embodied by the reproachful soul and the surah's pace.
rows.anchor: فجوابُ القسم محذوف ويُقَدِّرهُ النحاةُ (لتبعثن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering-bones question is tightly connected to the ending's question whether humanity will be left neglected.
rows.anchor: أنها مرتبطةٌ بما ورد في آخر السورة وهو قوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ الإنسان أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bala qadirin omits the governing verb, supplied by grammarians as We gather them while able; this omission also matches haste. Specific finger-bone shaping sits beside gathering bones, while general shaping appears with general creation later.
rows.anchor: وملاحظة أخرى في هذا التعبير، وهي أنه حذف منه عامل الحال، فقال: {بلى قَادِرِينَ} ولم يذكر عامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferring immediate life to the afterlife reflects the human disposition toward haste, shared across humanity, as also stated that the human was created in haste.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {خُلِقَ الإنسان مِنْ عَجَلٍ} [الأنبياء: 37]

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the address as universal: humans were made hasty, so they love the immediate and leave the afterlife; he connects the tongue instruction to this rebuke.
rows.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) في قوله تعالى: {كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ العاجلة}

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi connects love of the immediate and abandoning the afterlife to humans' haste, procrastination in repentance, false hope, and indulgence; the closest link is the desire to sin ahead.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (روح المعاني) في هذه الآية: {كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ العاجلة * وَتَذَرُونَ الآخرة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive an yufala biha suits a calamity decreed rather than accidental and avoids attributing evil directly to God, in keeping with other passages that do not ascribe evil to Him.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه لم يقل: (أن نفعل بها) بإسناد الفعل إلى ذاته العلية، لأنه لم يُرِدْ أن ينسبَ إيقاع هذه الكارثة والشر المستطير إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in balaghat refers to the soul although it was not mentioned; this omission, like other missing subjects, matches the surah's haste.
rows.anchor: والضمير في {بَلَغَتِ} للنفس وإن لم يَجْرِ لها ذِكْرٌ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive qila and its unnamed speaker fit the unstated soul and speaker at death; raq is deliberately ambiguous between someone reciting healing and someone ascending, matching the scene's obscurity.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الإبهام في (راق) مناسب لسياق الإبهام هذا، فإن كلمة (راق) مشتركة في كونها اسم فاعل للفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported explanation of the joining shanks is that they are wrapped together in the shroud.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه لَفُّهما في الكفن، وقيل: انتهاء أمرهما بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation is that the person's affair reaches its end in death; the author says both readings describe a death that certainly occurs.
rows.anchor: وكل ما قيل في تفسير الآية يراد به حالة من حالات الموت الذي حصل يقيناً لا ظناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting to your Lord makes Him the exclusive destination, and fronting on that day specifies the time of departure from worldly life; the destination is more important, so it comes first.
rows.anchor: فإن تقديم {إلى رَبِّكَ} يفيد القصر والاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masaq describes the soul's movement at death toward God, followed by the grave, which is only visited; mustaqarr in 75:12 describes the final abode after Resurrection, Paradise or Hell, where the journey ends.
rows.anchor: اختير لفظ (المساق) ههنا لأن الآية في مفارقة الروح الجسد عند الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denunciation after the death scene reports conditions of the afterlife, linking these verses to the opening oath by Resurrection.
rows.anchor: 1- أن هذه الآيات وقعت بعد قوله: {والتفت الساق بالساق * إلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ المساق} وهذا النفي والإخبار فيها، إنما هو في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer both commits denial and turns away, then leaves faith and prayer undone; the two kinds of failure provoke reproach for wrongful action and neglected good.
rows.anchor: والنفس هنا قدّمت التكذيب والتولّي: {ولاكن كَذَّبَ وتولى} وأخَّرت التصديقَ والصلاة {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person puts desires and sins first, connecting denial and turning away with the earlier account of wanting to continue sinning.
rows.anchor: ذلك أنه كذّب وتولى، فقدم شهواته ومعاصيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not believing in the Resurrection explains the person's failure to believe and pray; this links the conduct to his earlier question about when the Hour will come.
rows.anchor: فهو مستبعد له مكذب به فهو لم يصدق ولم يصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeds reported as sent ahead and left behind are disbelief and turning away on one side, and delayed faith and prayer on the other.
rows.anchor: فإنه قدم التكذيب والتولي وأخر التصديق والصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is inward assent, while belief and denial are matters of the heart, speech, and limbs: he lacked inward belief, openly denied, and turned away from action, so he lacked faith's reality.
rows.anchor: فهو لم يصدّق بالجنان {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ} وكذّب باللسان، كما قال تعالى: {ولاكن كَذَّبَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to pray and turning away connect with the later attempt to offer excuses when questioned about those deeds.
rows.anchor: وارتبط عدم الصلاة والتولي بإلقاء المعاذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His denial also links to the question about gathering bones, since belief in the Last Day is a central article of faith.
rows.anchor: والإيمان باليوم الآخر من أهم أركان الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person loves the immediate life and leaves the afterlife, which accounts for his denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: فكذّب وتولى وترك الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had he believed and prayed, he would have joined the radiant faces; because he denied and turned away, he belongs with the grim-faced people.
rows.anchor: لو صدق وصلى لكان من أصحاب الوجوه الناضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning outlines woe at death, at Resurrection, and on entering Hell, mapping successive punishments.
rows.anchor: والويلُ لك ميتاً، والويل لك يوم البعث، والويل لك يوم تدخل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa separates each pair of closely spaced punishments, while thumma marks the distant interval between worldly death, the grave, Resurrection, and Hell; immediate fa also matches the surah's haste theme.
rows.anchor: فكل عذابين قريبين من بعضهما فصل بينهما بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether humanity is left neglected links back to the oath, gathering bones, the record of deeds, the preceding threat, and the closing proof of God's power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية مرتبطة بأول السورة، وهو القَسم بيوم القيامة، ومرتبطة بقوله تعالى: {أَيَحْسَبُ الإنسان أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in minhu refers to male semen: the author asserts that the male determines whether the child is male or female, and the Quran stated this before modern genetics and embryology.
rows.anchor: والهاء في {مِنْهُ} تعود على المنيّ، فمن ماء الرجل يكون الذكر والأنثى، وليس للأنثى فيه دخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine min-ha would refer to the clot; referring back to semen instead avoids ambiguity, since the drop is part of the semen but the wording could otherwise point to the clot.
rows.anchor: ولم يُعده على النطفة مع أنها هي القطرة من المنيّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls this both a scientific and a rhetorical miracle.
rows.anchor: وهذا إعجاز علمي علاوة على الإعجاز الفني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspoken subject of laysa is the demonstrative dhalika, pointing to an unstated entity; this matches the omitted agents in preceding actions, and the ending echoes the opening's Resurrection oath.
rows.anchor: اسم (ليس) مكنيٌّ غير مصرّح به وهو اسم الإشارة (ذلك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the dead seems harder than reshaping fingertips to human reason, although all divine acts are equal; the question form and emphatic ba therefore underscore the importance of resurrection.
rows.anchor: إحياء الموتى أصعب وأعسر من تسوية البنان في القياس العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit bala qadirin affirms finger-shaping but omits its verb and circumstantial subject; the complete, emphatic question about reviving the dead marks its greater rhetorical weight.
rows.anchor: فدلَّ ذلك على الفرق بين المقامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is built around Resurrection, the reproachful soul, haste, and paired expressions; these are its organizing rhetorical strands.
rows.anchor: فالسورة مبنية عليهما أصلا كما بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haste appears through omitted elements: the oath's answer, the governing verb of qadirin, the antecedent of the tongue pronoun, and the unstated subject of balaghat.
rows.anchor: فمن مراعاة جانب العجلة: 1- حذف جواب القسم الذي افتتحت به السورة وهو {لاَ أُقْسِمُ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agent of neither believed nor prayed is omitted as another mark of the surah's haste.
rows.anchor: 6- عدم ذكر فاعل {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping the n from yakun in the question about a drop of semen is another instance of omission shaped by haste.
rows.anchor: حذف نون (يكون) في قوله: {أَلَمْ يَكُ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other scenes of haste include the desire to sin ahead, the instruction not to hurry the tongue, and preferring immediate life to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: 1- قوله: {بَلْ يُرِيدُ الإنسان لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ} والمعنى: أنه يؤثر العاجلة، فيقدم شهواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah repeatedly pairs opposites or corresponding matters: Resurrection with the reproachful soul, sun with moon, deeds advanced with delayed, inward self-knowledge with outward excuses, and immediate life with afterlife.
rows.anchor: فالسورة تبدأ بالقسم بشيئين هما: يوم القيامة، والنفس اللوامة، ثم تستمر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah pairs loving the immediate life with leaving the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وذكرت الحُبَّ والتَّرْكَ وذلك في قوله: {تُحِبُّونَ} و {وَتَذَرُونَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It pairs two kinds of faces, radiant and gloomy.
rows.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من الوجوه: الوجوه الناضرة، والوجوه الباسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It negates two acts of obedience: belief and prayer.
rows.anchor: ونفت اثنتين من الطاعات في قوله: {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It affirms two sins: denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: وأثبتت اثنتين من المعاصي وذلك في قوله: {ولاكن كَذَّبَ وتولى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It repeats the same warning formula twice.
rows.anchor: وكررت آية واحدة مرتين وهي قوله: {أولى لَكَ فأولى * ثُمَّ أولى لَكَ فأولى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise receive two blessings: radiant faces and looking toward their Lord.
rows.anchor: وذكرت نعمتين من نعم أهل الجنة: نضرة الوجوه والنظر إلى الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Hell face two punishments: gloomy faces and a back-breaking calamity.
rows.anchor: وذكرت عقوبتين من عقوبات أهل النار، بُسور الوجه وقاصمة الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah describes gathering on Judgment Day in gathering bones and sun with moon, and earthly gathering in collecting and reciting the Quran.
rows.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من الجمع، جمعاً في يوم القيامة وجمعاً في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It pairs divine power to shape fingertips with power to revive the dead, using direct affirmation for the first and an interrogative affirmation for the second.
rows.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من القدرة: القدرة على تسوية البنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah contrasts restricted, partial shaping of fingertips with the unrestricted, general shaping of creation.
rows.anchor: وذكر نوعين من التسوية: تسوية جزئية مقيدة وهي تسوية البنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It names two stages of human creation, the semen drop and the clot.
rows.anchor: وذكر طورين من أطوار خلق الإنسان، وهما النطفة والعلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It names the two sexes, male and female.
rows.anchor: وذكر الجنسين وهما الذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is described with plural forms such as We are able, We gather, and We shape, as well as singular forms such as He created and proportioned.
rows.anchor: التعبير بالجمع {بلى قَادِرِينَ} و {نَّجْمَعَ} و {نُّسَوِّيَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Balad names the orphan and poor also mentioned in al-Fajr, answering the earlier charge that people fail to honor orphans or urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: ووصف الله الإنسان بأنه لا يكرم اليتيم، ولا يحضّ على طعام المسكين في سورة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since al-Fajr condemns intense love of wealth and devouring inheritance, al-Balad says overcoming the obstacle requires sharing wealth with others.
rows.anchor: يحب المال حبا شديدا ويأكل التراث أكلا لما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relation between eating inheritance and feeding during famine is direct: just as people eat, they should feed others.
rows.anchor: كما يأكل ينبغي أن يطعم الآخرين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says al-Balad follows al-Fajr's discussion of testing people through ease and hardship, their blameworthy traits, and the fates of people and believers.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى ابتلاءه للإنسان بحالة التنعيم

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the passage answers condemnation of loving wealth, consuming inheritance, and neglecting the poor by naming what wealth holders should do: free captives and feed people during famine.
rows.anchor: ولما ذم سبحانه فيما قبلها من أحب المال

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi adds that freeing captives and feeding during famine are virtues expected of a wealthy person, just as the previous surah mentioned the contented soul and this one describes what brings contentment.
rows.anchor: وعلا فيها الخصال التي تطلب من صاحب المال من فك الرقبة، وإطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Balad comprehensively presents the elements of a message: Mecca, its resident Messenger, humanity as recipients, faith and good works as the message, and believers and disbelievers as the two response groups.
rows.anchor: استوفت عناصر البلاغ والإرسال، فقد ذكرت موطن الرسالة، والرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears that humanity was created immersed in struggle and hardship.
rows.anchor: على أن الإنسان خُلق مغموراً في مكابدة الشدائد والصعاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by the sacred city while the Messenger lives there and conveys his call.
rows.anchor: فقد أقسم سبحانه بالبلد الحرام في حال حلول الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing hill rather than the ordinary word for residing gathers several intended meanings at once; one sense is that the Prophet is residing in Mecca.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن كلمة {حِلٌّ} تحتمل معاني عدة: منها: أنها تأتي بمعنى الحالّ والمقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's presence adds a second honor to Mecca's sacred honor, so his residence makes the city more worthy of the oath.
rows.anchor: وهو أنه لما حل الرسول بمكة جمعت شرفين، شرفها هي

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the oath honors Mecca for both its sacred status and the Messenger's presence and residence there.
rows.anchor: إنه تعالى أقسم بها لما جمعت من الشرفين شرفها بإضافتها إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Prophet's presence shows his great merit and that a place gains honor from the standing of its people.
rows.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بالبلد الحرام، وقَيَّده بحلوله عليه السلام فيه

rows.speaker: التبيان في أقسام القرآن
rows.claim: Al-Tibyan says the resident reading adds that God's town contains His Messenger and servant, the best place holding the best of servants and guide to people.
rows.anchor: إنه إذا كان الحل من الحلول، فهو متضمن لهذا التعظيم
